recruit_text.greeting: You want someone who hits things, or someone who hits things first? They're different rates. I'll quote you the second and do the first, and I'll call it a discount.
recruit_text.before:
Five years of cargo manifests and camera feeds at the Port of Antwerp, and the dockside arrangement where everybody took a little and nobody took enough to become a problem.

He didn't join in, and he didn't report it either. Ask him what he believed in back then and he'd have changed the subject, quickly.

There's nobody he's looking for, he says. He mentions that more often than a man who meant it would.

stages.stranger: Name's Silas, and I notice things for a living, which crate's light, which captain's lying, who's about to rob who. What did I do before? It was port work. Ask me again tomorrow and it'll be different port work.
stages.acquaintance: Fine, the true version. Antwerp, near the docks. My dad was an English sailor who was home three months a year and then not at all, and my mum raised us on a cleaner's wage. I drifted through my twenties, then I got five years as a security guard at the port, watching cameras and checking manifests. First steady job of my life.
stages.companion: The docks had an arrangement where everybody took a little. I never joined in and I never said anything. I landed in Ratchet on a night shift with this coin in my pocket, and I was delighted. No record, no reputation, nothing to live down. I'm embarrassed about that now. I flip the coin for anything I don't want to decide, which is most things.
stages.friend: I've got a brother, Jens, four years younger. He did join in at the port, and he got in deep, and I watched it happen on the cameras for months and said nothing. He did two years. We hadn't spoken since the trial. A sailor here says there's a young Belgian working the docks at Booty Bay, quick with numbers and in some trouble. I'm not flipping a coin on this one. Will you come?
stages.sworn: I told Jens about the cameras, on the pier after. He said he always knew, and he'd have done it anyway, and he was angry for a long time and he isn't now. We had a beer. He's in Ratchet with me now. And I've taken a cut of the goblin's pier, my first real commitment, and I didn't flip the coin to decide it. You can have the coin. I'd rather you had it than be tempted.

moments.prompt: At the end of his first trip with you, he flips his coin.
moments.line: Heads I stay, tails I go back to Ratchet. Let's see what it says.

options.reply: Huh, nobody's ever asked me not to flip it. All right, I'll stay.
It came up tails, so I'll see you in Ratchet, then. It was fun.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about Jens and the cameras.

options.reply: Yeah, that's the whole plan, really. Let's go and do it.
I could've tried. That's the bit I keep coming back to.

lines.bored_warning: I'm built for docks and doors, not fields. Find me a crowd and I'll be useful.
lines.leaving_good: Forty things noticed and most of them sellable. I'm heading back to Ratchet. You know which pier.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm off back to Ratchet. This has gone stale, and I don't do stale.
lines.after_wipe: Well, somebody read that wrong, and for once it wasn't me. Let's look at it properly.
lines.wipe_warning: I don't like the odds in here, and they're not improving. One more, then I'm making myself scarce.
lines.wipe_leave: I've stuck it out, which isn't like me. I'll be in Ratchet getting some air.
lines.zone_warning: I can read a room, and this whole place is telling us to leave. I'd listen to it.
lines.zone_leave: The room said leave, and I'm leaving. I'll be on the middle pier in Ratchet.
lines.gear_refuse: No chance, that's mine. Nice try, though.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, take it. I'll remember who's got it, though, I remember everything.
lines.gear_short: You've still not put anything back in that spot, in case you were hoping I'd forgotten.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's nice work. Thanks. I'll pretend I'm not touched.
lines.back: I've heard some things in Ratchet you'll want to know. They'll cost you a drink.
lines.send_word: Silas has sent word from Ratchet. He's heard a few things and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I want to say straight why I went, which isn't my strong suit. Give me a minute and I'll do it properly.
lines.neglect: Well, look who's come back. I'd started reading the room for signs of you, and the room had nothing.
lines.asked_to_stay: One more's free. No coin needed.
lines.on_break: Silas is back on the middle pier in Ratchet. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.mail_yes: You'll find me in {town}. I'll be the one in the corner who already knows what you're going to ask.
lines.mail_later: I'm in the middle of something that doesn't care for interruptions. Do your rounds and I'll turn up when it's done.
lines.mail_see_me: Some things I only say out loud, and only once. Come to Ratchet. You know which pier.

town_arrive.text: Three ways out of this square, and two of them are bad.
Somebody here's already pricing our boots.
My mum raised us on a cleaner's wage near the docks, and she could make a week's food out of nothing. Towns like this make me think of her.

dungeon_clear.text: Nothing down there was locked. That bothers me more than if it had been.

boss_down.text: Check its hands before anybody checks its pockets.

zone_arrive.text: Two ways out of here that I can see. I like to know.
